system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Preliminary review for negotiation; to be confirmed with NSW transaction counsel before issuing a mark-up.

## 1. Overall assessment

The Seller's cover note describes the package as "fair and balanced." It is not. The Seller Update pushes almost every risk-allocation lever to the seller-friendly extreme, and – importantly – the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts several of the reassuring statements in the Seller Update (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay). Those contradictions are useful leverage: the Seller has itself documented that the key completion items are **not** in place.

The structural theme is that the Seller is trying to collapse every category of claim (title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, fraud) into one low general-warranty regime, then neutralise that regime through broad disclosure and constructive-knowledge clauses. We should resist the architecture, not just the numbers.

## 2. Material issues, in priority order

### A. Fundamental/title warranties subject to the 20% cap and 18-month limit (Cl 12.1, 12.3, "Fundamental/Title")

**Departure:** The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties sit under the same AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month notice period as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."

**Why it matters:** We are paying AUD 24m for shares. If title fails, we lose the whole price, not 20% of it. Title and capacity warranties are conventionally capped at 100% of price and run for 6–7 years (the NSW contract limitation period, or longer if the SPA is a deed – it should be). "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.

**Push back:** Separate tier of Fundamental Warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, share capital) – cap = purchase price, time limit = 7 years or no limit, not subject to de minimis/basket, not qualified by disclosure or Buyer knowledge.

### B. Limitations applied "to all Claims of any nature" (Cl 9.3, 12.3, 12.8, 20.5)

**Departure:** (i) Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise; (ii) the caps, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to Claims "of any nature."

**Why it matters:** This would sweep the specific indemnities (Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006), any tax indemnity, leakage/debt-free-cash-free adjustments, covenants (e.g., Riverlark release), and fraud into the AUD 4.8m / 18-month / basket regime. It also reverses the drafting burden – silence favours the Seller.

**Push back:**
- Delete the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default. Limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.
- Express carve-outs from all caps/thresholds/time limits: fraud, wilful concealment, Fundamental Warranties, Tax Warranties/Tax Indemnity, specific indemnities, leakage/completion adjustments, and breach of Seller covenants.
- Exclusive-remedy clause must preserve injunctive/specific performance relief and the indemnities.
- Non-reliance: note that liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under s 18 ACL cannot be contracted out of; the clause should be confined to pre-contractual statements not repeated in the SPA and must not purport to exclude statutory claims. Resist any wording that goes further.

### C. Debt-free/cash-free not delivered – Riverlark AUD 3.2m facility (Cl 2/7; DL para 3)

**Departure:** The Seller proposes the Riverlark facility be dealt with by "a release to be provided following Completion." Its own Disclosure Letter confirms the facility is unpaid, no discharge is in the data room, and the facility has change-of-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions.

**Why it matters:** This is flatly inconsistent with the agreed debt-free/cash-free basis. Completion with the facility outstanding means (a) the Buyer effectively pays AUD 27.2m, (b) Completion itself may trigger an event of default under 8.1, and (c) any security over the shares or assets remains in place – which also undermines title (Issue A).

**Push back:**
- Riverlark repayment is a Completion deliverable: payoff letter from Riverlark fixing the amount, repayment from the Seller's proceeds via the funds flow, executed deed of release and PPSR discharge (and release of any share mortgage) delivered **at** Completion.
- Alternatively, deduct the payoff amount from the price with the Buyer paying Riverlark directly.
- Seller warranty and indemnity that no other financial debt exists at Completion.
- Run a PPSR search now; confirm whether Harbourglass has granted any security over the Paperbark shares.

### D. Bluefen consent (Cl 3/6.3; DL para 2) – ~30% of revenue

**Departure:** The Seller Update says the consent "is addressed" and will be "treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent," on a reasonable-endeavours basis. The Disclosure Letter says no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions have been satisfied.

**Why it matters:** AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue is exposed to a change-of-control right. A consent that is conditional (cl 11.3) is not a consent. "Reasonable endeavours" on the Seller's part with no Buyer approval right over the form of consent is weak for an item this size.

**Push back:**
- Hard condition precedent: unconditional written consent from Bluefen (or written evidence that all 11.3 conditions are satisfied), in a form approved by the Buyer (acting reasonably), with no adverse changes to the Bluefen contract.
- Seller obligation: best (or all reasonable) endeavours; Buyer entitled to participate in Bluefen discussions.
- Longstop date and Buyer termination right; no waiver by Seller.
- Fallback if the Seller resists a hard CP: price retention/escrow or deferred consideration tied to Bluefen revenue retention for 12 months post-Completion, plus a specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates for change of control.

### E. Funds flow and the DD-005 closing bonuses (AUD 420,000 + on-costs)

**Departure:** The Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow; the Disclosure Letter confirms they are triggered by Completion, are not in the funds flow, and is silent on super, payroll tax and on-costs.

**Why it matters:** If the bonuses are payable by the Company, they are a Completion-triggered liability the Buyer inherits – a transaction cost that belongs to the Seller. The true cost is larger than AUD 420k: add superannuation (12% from 1 July 2025) and NSW payroll tax (5.45%), roughly AUD 490k+ all-in. The "continued-employment" conditions also need to be understood – if there is a post-Completion retention tail, part of the benefit accrues to the Buyer and that part can legitimately be shared, but the Completion-triggered portion should not.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses (grossed up for super, payroll tax and any other on-costs) as Transaction Costs/Debt-like items deducted from the price or paid by the Seller through the funds flow at Completion.
- Specific indemnity for any Completion-triggered employee payments not so deducted.
- Obtain the bonus letters and confirm whether any other change-of-control payments or accelerated equity exist.

### F. Ironquay IP (Cl 11.1; DL para 4)

**Departure:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000 per DD-010) and described as "adequate."

**Why it matters:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee. Until paid, the Company does not own the IP in those deliverables. For an analytics business, the exposure is loss of/clouded title to product IP, infringement claims, and re-procurement cost – not the AUD 180k invoice. The Seller also concedes there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.

**Push back:**
- Completion deliverables: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay to the Company (ideally a CP).
- Indemnity extended to all Loss arising from the Company not holding unencumbered title to the SOW3 Project Materials (including third-party claims and replacement costs), outside the general cap and basket.
- Full IP ownership warranties (not "settled under the general regime" – see Issue I).

### G. DD-006 data export incident (Cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL para 6)

**Departure:** The Seller characterises this as a "preliminary operational matter … not expected to be material."

**Why it matters:** ~1,240 records of personal information sent to an unintended external recipient is a potential eligible data breach under the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme. The Company is obliged to assess within 30 days and, if there is likely serious harm, notify the OAIC and affected individuals. The incident is recorded at 22 September; it is now 6 November, so the assessment window has already run. Exposure includes OAIC enforcement (penalties were increased substantially in 2022–24), the statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy (in force since June 2025), customer-contract breach-notification obligations (check Bluefen), and reputational harm to a data business. "No loss amount stated" is not the same as no loss.

**Push back:**
- Pre-Completion covenant: complete the assessment, obtain the recipient's deletion confirmation, and make any required notifications, with Buyer consultation rights on OAIC/customer communications.
- Specific indemnity for all Loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification costs, third-party claims, remediation), outside the general cap/basket, with a longer time limit.
- Privacy/data warranties not qualified by DL para 6 beyond the facts actually stated.
- Consider a specific CP if the assessment reveals a notifiable breach with customer-contract consequences.

### H. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge (Sch 7; Cl 8.3; DL paras 1.1–1.4)

**Departure:** (i) General disclosure of the entire data room and "publicly searchable corporate records"; (ii) the Buyer has no claim for anything it or its advisers knew **or could have discovered** from the data room or public records; (iii) disclosure is frozen at 22 September 2026.

**Why it matters:** Combined, these two clauses gut the warranty package. "Discoverable from public records" is constructive knowledge of every ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia, court and land-registry record. "Advisers' knowledge" imputes to the Buyer whatever any associate at any adviser saw. Blanket data-room disclosure means a single line buried in a 300-page contract defeats a claim.

**Push back:**
- Disclosure standard: only matters **fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter (and expressly indexed data room documents) with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely impact. No general disclosure of public registers; at most, disclosure of specified searches (ASIC, PPSR) conducted on a stated date, with results annexed.
- Delete cl 8.3. If a knowledge qualifier must survive, limit it to actual knowledge of two or three named Buyer deal-team individuals of a matter **and** of the fact that it constitutes a breach – no constructive knowledge, no adviser knowledge, no "discoverable."
- Warranties repeated at Completion; Seller may deliver a supplementary disclosure for signing-to-Completion events only, which does not qualify warranties for claim purposes but entitles the Buyer to terminate if material.
- DL para 1.4 (non-admission) is standard, but confirm it does not prevent the stated facts being relied on as fair disclosure in the Buyer's favour.

### I. Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime"

**Departure:** 20% cap, 18 months, basket applies.

**Why it matters:** The ATO amendment period is generally 4 years (longer in cases of fraud/evasion), so an 18-month tax warranty is meaningless. For an analytics company, IP is the asset being bought.

**Push back:** Separate Tax Indemnity (pre-Completion tax, pound-for-pound, no basket) and Tax Warranties: cap at purchase price, 7 years. IP Warranties: higher cap (we would open at 50–100% of price) and 3–4 year period, not qualified by general data-room disclosure.

### J. Quantum and thresholds (Cl 12.1, 12.2, 12.3)

- **General cap 20% (AUD 4.8m):** For a private deal of this size without W&I insurance, 30–50% is a reasonable opening position; 20% is at the seller-friendly end. If the Seller holds at 20%, consider whether a W&I policy changes the economics (in which case the seller cap could be low but the buyer gets insurer cover).
- **De minimis AUD 25k (~0.1%) and basket AUD 250k (~1%):** The percentages are within market, but (i) the basket should be a **tipping** basket (recover from dollar one once exceeded), not a deductible; (ii) related claims arising from the same facts should aggregate for de minimis purposes; (iii) neither threshold should apply to Fundamental/Tax claims or the specific indemnities.
- **18 months:** Push to 24 months, which captures a full audit cycle post-Completion. Notified claims should survive if proceedings are commenced within 6–9 months of notice.

### K. Lesser items

- **Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k; DD-008/DD-011):** Three related AUD 110k renewals that the Seller asks us to "read together" look like a single AUD 330k commitment split to sit under an approval threshold. Confirm whether they are signed or pending; if pending, they should require Buyer consent under the interim conduct covenants; if already committed and above-market or avoidable, treat as a price/working-capital item. Seller's own letter refuses to say whether they are ordinary course.
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Notification obligation – add as a Seller pre-Completion covenant with evidence of notice as a Completion deliverable. Confirm there is no change-of-control right by reviewing the lease directly.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller's position (assignment restriction not triggered by share sale) is plausible but should be verified against the actual change-of-control definition. Warranty that no consents are required other than those listed in a schedule.
- **Title (DD-012; DL para 10):** The Seller is relying only on the Company share register and expressly says the Buyer has not verified. We should run our own ASIC and PPSR searches, review the constitution for pre-emptive rights, and confirm no options/convertibles. This does not reduce the Seller's warranty obligation – the title warranty must be absolute and unqualified by disclosure.
- **Disclosure Letter cut-off (22 Sept 2026):** Six weeks old. Require an updated letter at signing and a bring-down at Completion (see Issue H).

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Recommended Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fundamental/title warranties | Separate tier: cap = 100% of price; 7 years; no basket/de minimis; not disclosure- or knowledge-qualified |
| 2 | "All Claims" limitation / exclusive remedy / non-reliance | Delete default; express carve-outs for fraud, fundamental, tax, specific indemnities, leakage, covenants; preserve ACL and equitable relief |
| 3 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Repay from Seller proceeds at Completion via funds flow; payoff letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge as Completion deliverables; otherwise price deduction |
| 4 | Bluefen consent | Hard CP: unconditional consent in Buyer-approved form; best endeavours; longstop and termination right; fallback escrow/indemnity |
| 5 | DD-005 bonuses | Treat AUD 420k + super + payroll tax as Transaction Costs deducted from price or paid by Seller; specific indemnity |
| 6 | Ironquay IP | Payment evidence and confirmatory assignment as Completion deliverables; indemnity covers loss of IP title, not just AUD 180k; full IP warranties |
| 7 | DD-006 incident | Pre-Completion assessment/notification covenant with Buyer consultation; uncapped specific indemnity; privacy warranties |
| 8 | Disclosure standard | "Fairly disclosed" standard; no blanket data-room or public-register disclosure; updated letter at signing and bring-down at Completion |
| 9 | Cl 8.3 Buyer knowledge | Delete; at most actual knowledge of named individuals of the breach |
| 10 | Tax / IP | Separate tax indemnity and warranties (price cap, 7 years); IP warranties with higher cap and longer period |
| 11 | General cap / thresholds / time | Open at 30–50% cap; tipping basket; aggregate related claims; 24 months; consider W&I |
| 12 | Sandbar, lease, Mossvale, title | Consent for pending renewals; lease notice deliverable; verify Mossvale change-of-control wording; run own ASIC/PPSR searches without diluting title warranty |

**Negotiation note:** Lead with Issues 3, 4 and 5 – these are not "market" debates but failures to deliver the agreed debt-free/cash-free basis and the agreed commercial foundation (Bluefen revenue), and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter supports our position on each. Hold the structural points (Issues 1, 2, 8, 9) as non-negotiable; trade on quantum (Issue 11) if needed.
=== END ADVICE ===
